messages:
oncall-bot: Incident detected: abnormal GPU memory growth on kv-cache shards; alert: repeated OOMs on host infer-gpu-07. Count: 19 OOMs in 5m.

sarah: seeing repeated `cuda alloc failed` logs + continuous-batch queue spiking.

kai: looks like KV cache size jumped from ~18GB -> ~72GB on shard-7. probable fragmentation / allocator degrowth. sample logs:
```
[2026-04-10T14:05:12Z] kv_cache: arena_alloc failed for 32768 bytes at 0x7fffa23c
[2026-04-10T14:05:13Z] pytorch: CUDA out of memory trying to allocate 32.0 MiB
[2026-04-10T14:05:13Z] continuous_batch: queue_depth spiked to 640
```

lee: oncall responding, taking triage. tagging infra and runtime.

alice: @lee can you run per-shard memory metrics? `curl -s http://metrics/api/query?metric=kv_cache_bytes&shard=7`

lee: ran quick checks: `redis info memory` equivalent shows fragmentation_ratio=2.9, arena_cnt=64. ptmalloc stats show many small free blocks but arenas not returned.

bryan: fragmentation ratio >2.5 suggests arenas are pinned. continuous-batching increase could be driving long-lived cache entries that prevent coalescing.

kai: any deploys or config changes before spike? we rolled continuous-batch max_batch from 256 -> 512 at 13:12 UTC.

sarah: confirmed, rollout started 13:12 and saw first OOMs ~13:55. correlation looks strong.

support-bot: customer-impact: 3 enterprise customers reporting increased 95p latency and intermittent timeouts on generation endpoints. No complete data loss reported. Statuspage notified: incident status = investigating.

lee: mitigation plan candidate: 1) rollback batch limits (max_batch -> 256), 2) throttle prefix prefetch, 3) rolling restart to reclaim GPU contexts and free arenas, 4) enable aggressive allocator purge if available.

alice: we can push runtime config change without full image roll via config service. patch payload ready: `{
  "continuous_batch.max_batch": 256,
  "continuous_batch.batch_window_ms": 5,
  "kv_cache.prefetch": false
}`

kai: applying patch to shard-group 7 now. kicking hotfix id cfg-20260410-001.

oncall-bot: Deploy started: config-change cfg-20260410-001 by kai.

bryan: also recommend restarting one worker pod to reset CUDA contexts. avoid mass restarts. I'll coordinate rolling restart one at a time.

sarah: initiating rolling restart: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/infer-worker -l shard=7 --max-unavailable=1`. starting pod-07-a.

ops-bot: Restart succeeded: pod infer-worker-07-a -> ready. uptime previous 4d.

alice: quick metric check after config + first restart: kv_cache_bytes down ~55% over 3m, fragmentation_ratio trending to ~1.4, continuous-batch queue depth normalized. OOM count dropped to 0 in last 10m.

support-bot: status update posted: mitigation in progress; customers notified of improvement.

kai: leaving canary watch for 30m. if stable we'll apply same config to other shard-groups. we should also evaluate changing default runtime allocator (consider jemalloc) and reducing arena_count.

bryan: opening follow-up PM ticket P-2026-042: investigate allocator fragmentation pattern, continuous-batch sizing safety guardrails, add alert on per-shard kv_cache growth rate > 3x in 10m.

lee: handoff: I'm handing primary to @kai at 14:30 UTC for follow-up engineering investigation and postmortem. I will remain available.

kai: taking over. immediate next actions: bake jemalloc runtime image, run load tests with max_batch=512 and prefetch=false, and propose new batch default 256 with autoscale.

sarah: thanks all. incident state: mitigated. notes: avoid large batch parameter rollouts during peak traffic windows; add rollout canary stage and circuit breaker for kv_cache growth.

support-bot: final customer update sent: degraded latency resolved, engineering investigating root cause; next update planned in 24h.

oncall-bot: Incident mitigated (cfg-20260410-001) — autoclosed by oncall-bot after 45m.
